taxonomy.note: Older nursery, horticultural, and Texas references frequently use Conoclinium greggii.

project_tracker_diagnostic: Rhizomatous perennial with ovate-deltate leaves that are deeply lobed/dissected, and fuzzy lavender-blue to purple discoid flower heads.

project_inclusion.learning_reason: Very useful Central Texas mistflower and an important current-name/synonym lesson.

morphology_keys.habit: Erect to spreading perennial, often arising from knotty crowns and capable of forming colonies.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite; blades ovate-deltate to ovate, roughly 1.5–4 cm, with margins distinctly lobed or dissected.
morphology_keys.heads: Small discoid heads; florets lavender-blue to purple, without ray florets.
morphology_keys.phyllaries: About 3.5–5 mm in Flora of North America.
morphology_keys.fruit: Cypselae about 1.8–2.5 mm with a bristly pappus.
best_field_traits: Joey's source under the familiar name Conoclinium greggii shows the low mounded/spreading landscape habit—use that habit with the deeply dissected leaves, not flower color alone.
morphology_keys.joey_field_note: Joey's West Texas landscaping video labels this plant Conoclinium greggii; the project reconciles that familiar older name to accepted Conoclinium dissectum. The frame is most useful for mounded growth habit and whole-plant architecture.
morphology_keys.reproductive_confirmation: FNA: corollas 2.5–3.5 mm; cypselae 1.8–2.5 mm hispidulous.

photo_strategy.selection_logic: Use accepted iNaturalist taxon Conoclinium dissectum; prefer curated references plus several views from one Central Texas/Texas observation.

look_here_first: Check fully expanded middle leaves: deep lobes or dissections interrupt the leaf outline; opposite foliage and blue-violet rayless heads support Conoclinium. C. coelestinum has a simple toothed—not deeply cut—leaf outline.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Versus C. coelestinum: deeply dissected/lobed leaf vs intact toothed margin (PRIMARY); FNA fruit hispidulous 1.8–2.5 mm vs glabrous 1–1.5 mm (confirmation). Versus Chromolaena odorata: Conoclinium has shorter hemispheric involucres with 2–3 phyllary series, rather than cylindrical 8–10 mm and 4–6+ series.

diagnostic_photo_requirements.shot: one flattened mature middle stem leaf, upper and underside, with ruler
diagnostic_photo_requirements.must_show: depth of lobing/dissection and basal veins

diagnostic_photo_requirements.shot: ripe cypsela with millimeter scale at 10x or macro
one individual involucre sideways, scale and clear phyllaries
diagnostic_photo_requirements.must_show: phyllary series and rounded/hemispheric head base
